cases.title: Plain COPY of pit P3 (no Settings change): the copy gets its own number and the Check levels sentence, P3 keeps its label, and one U brings back the same objects
cases.plan_item: COPY of a pit (daily card D15); BUG-665 control route, ordinary COPY
cases.expected: COPY of pit P3 (handle 109D56) by 0,-5000 prints "1 pit copied and numbered as new. Check levels: they came across from the originals (the Inspector shows which ones to confirm).", adds one pit block and one PIT LABEL reading a P number that is not P3, the original label 109E08 still reads P3 before, after the COPY and after the U, and one U brings the drawing back to 1034 objects with the same handles in every one of its three chunks. The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The copy clean-up runs when AutoCAD ends the native COPY on the live drawing.
not_automated: DERIVED (29 Oct 2026 fix-up, Opus B6 review item 5): the copy reading exactly P8 is taken from the first free number on this test drawing (the other pit numbers on DRV1_B1 are P1 to P7, P9 and P10 and C1, so P8 is the one gap; a brand-new pit on this drawing also reads P8 in case N05), not from a card line that guarantees P8. The number is not compared against a live read of every pit label. The copy's levels (the Check levels content) and the Pit Schedule cells are not read. ROTATE Copy, SCALE Copy and grip Ctrl-drag are R34, R34s, R34so and R34sn. The handle comparison is fixture-specific (1034 objects); a general sorted-set reader would be better.

cases.title: With the Settings tick "Clean up grip Ctrl-drag, ROTATE Copy and SCALE Copy like COPY" switched ON, the copies of pit P3 made by COPY and by SCALE Copy each carry a pit number of their own (not P3) (the ROTATE Copy adds no label to read: see R34s)
cases.plan_item: BUG-665 part only: the COPY and SCALE Copy labels each read a P number other than P3, switch ON; D15 is case R34a
cases.expected: With the tick ON when AutoCAD starts, the PIT LABEL of the COPY and of the SCALE Copy of pit P3 each reads a pit number that is not P3 (the ROTATE Copy label count is recorded, not judged). The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The number is given by the live COPY / ROTATE / SCALE clean-up and read back from the PIT LABEL block in the real drawing.
not_automated: DERIVED (29 Oct 2026 fix-up, Opus B6 review item 6): the COPY label reading exactly P8 is taken from the first free number on this test drawing (the other pit numbers on DRV1_B1 are P1 to P7, P9 and P10 and C1, so P8 is the one gap), not from a card line that guarantees P8; the SCALE label is only checked to differ from P3 and from the COPY label (P8), so the two copies cannot share a number. The ROTATE Copy of pit P3 about its own centre (the route R34 uses) adds NO PIT LABEL even with the tick ON (run b3v1, 25 Oct 2026), so its number cannot be read: that is R34s's red, and the label count is only recorded here. Grip Ctrl-drag copy is not driven. Which number each copy should get (P12, P13, ...) is not asserted: only that it is a number of its own.
